prize_parts.citation: for theories of firm heterogeneity and selection that explain who exports, how resources are reallocated across firms, and how trade generates gains

statement.case_for: The heterogeneous-firm framework moved trade analysis from representative sectors to firm-level selection and reallocation, and it set the empirical agenda for firm-level trade research. It is both a discovery and an explanatory framework, which is the combination I value: it explains patterns that firm-level data revealed, and it generated testable predictions that have been confirmed across many countries over more than two decades. Attribution is also tighter than in my opening first choice. Melitz (2003) is the clear origin, and Helpman's work with Melitz and Yeaple on exports versus foreign direct investment is a natural complement. A two-person award therefore captures the core credit without an arbitrary cut. The 2008 prize covered the earlier new trade theory, so this is a distinct, later advance. The topic is mature, and it connects to productivity, reallocation and growth beyond trade.
statement.case_against: Credit for the firm-heterogeneity agenda is shared with Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are not on this ballot, and a two-person prize could be read as under-crediting the empirical foundation. Krugman's 2008 prize may also make some members feel the trade field is already covered. Quantitative welfare conclusions depend on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity and CES demand. The contribution is also more theoretical than the quasi-experimental evidence behind B038, which is closer to my own empirical priors, so I want to guard against over-weighting familiarity.

responses.point: Boppart ranked B025 third and argued that credit is spread across at least eight people, so any trio leaves out serious contributors and no selection is uncontroversial.
responses.response: I agree, and it is the main reason I am moving B025 from first to an alternative. I listed Calvo, Taylor and Woodford, while Boppart listed Taylor, Woodford and Gali. That we disagree on the third name shows the credit boundary is unsettled, not just that the three-name cap is inconvenient. I still think the scientific importance is very large. But a prize whose laureate set the committee cannot defend is weaker than one with a clean core. Boppart also ranked B044 second with the same Melitz and Helpman pair, so we agree there on attribution.

responses.point: Enflo ranked B044 first and saw Melitz (2003) as central with Helpman as the natural complement. She flagged that Krugman's 2008 prize may reduce appetite and that Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are an attribution issue.
responses.response: I agree that Redding is better described as an extender of the framework, so I would not add a third name. On Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, I think the committee should define the award as the theoretical framework of selection and reallocation, not the whole firm-level trade agenda. Their empirical documentation of exporter heterogeneity is closely related, but the integrated general-equilibrium model is what changed the field's analysis of gains from trade. I do not claim that boundary is free of dispute and I list it as an uncertainty. On Krugman, I read the 2008 prize as recognising the earlier increasing-returns and scale-based trade theory. This work changed the unit of analysis and is distinct enough not to count as repetition.

responses.point: Hassler ranked B044 third, with Melitz pivotal and Helpman's firm-level work substantial. He noted that Helpman's credit could be split across other candidacies and that quantitative gains-from-trade results depend on structural assumptions. He also left Katz out of his B038 trio because the skill-biased-change work overlaps with the 2023 prize.
responses.response: I accept the structural-assumption point and treat it as the main scientific reservation. The qualitative predictions of selection into exporting and reallocation are well confirmed, while the size of the welfare gains is model-dependent. Whether the prize rewards the mechanism or the magnitudes matters for the citation, and I word it around the mechanism. On Helpman's other candidacy, I would credit him here for the firm-heterogeneity work with Melitz and not use another candidacy to dilute it. On B038, I only partly share the Katz concern. As I understand it, the 2023 prize was for Goldin's work on women's labour-market outcomes, so the skill-premium and wage-structure contribution was not itself recognised. That keeps B038 a credible alternative with Katz, though I would not call it as clean as B044.

responses.point: Fredriksson ranked B038 first, calling the task framework and China-shock evidence transformative for theory, empirics and policy. He saw a Hanson-over-Dorn choice as a judgement call and noted that the China-shock estimates are debated.
responses.response: I agree that B038 is a serious contender and I ranked it third. My reservations concern attribution. The task framework draws on contributors outside this ballot, and the three-name cap forces out Dorn, whose co-authorship on the China-shock papers is central. Because the shift-share identification and the persistence of the effects are still debated, I give B038 less weight on maturity than B044, where the main predictions have been tested repeatedly. I would not claim B044 is more important to society. I weigh the cleaner credit boundary more heavily, and I would support B038 if the committee finds a convincing way to credit Dorn.

uncertainties: Whether the committee should define the discovery narrowly, as the Melitz and Helpman theoretical framework, or broadly enough to include Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are not credited on this ballot.
Whether Krugman's 2008 prize lowers the committee's appetite for another trade award, and whether it should.
How much weight to put on gains-from-trade magnitudes that depend on functional-form assumptions, compared with the qualitative selection mechanism.

Whether B038 or B025 would have a more defensible credit boundary if members converge on a particular trio. This is based on my reading of colleagues' openings, not independent verification of the literatures.
statement.conflict_note: none apparent from the supplied profile. My co-authors and research field (labour economics and the economics of crime) do not overlap with the credited names on B044, and I do not see a connection to the alternatives either.
